topic: Wearing someone else's glasses: harmful? Myth vs fact

youtube.title: Wearing someone else's glasses: harmful? 👓 Myth vs Fact #Shorts
youtube.description:
Is it harmful to wear someone else's glasses? Here's the myth vs the fact.
மற்றவர் கண்ணாடியை போட்டால் கண் பாதிக்குமா?

• Myth: borrowed glasses permanently damage your eyes. Fact: no lasting damage, but they can cause headache, eye strain and blur.
• Every lens is made for one person's power AND the distance between their pupils (PD).
• Many people have a different power in each eye, or cylinder power for astigmatism, so a borrowed pair rarely matches.
• Ready-made reading glasses are the same power in both eyes; they're not a substitute for a proper eye test.
• Children should never use an elder's glasses; kids' eyes need their own checked power.
• If your own glasses feel blurry, your power may have changed. Get it rechecked.

gmb.text: Is it harmful to wear someone else's glasses? It's a common myth that borrowed glasses permanently damage your eyes. In fact, they don't cause lasting damage, but they can cause headaches, eye strain and blurred vision. Every lens is made for one person's power and the distance between their pupils, and many people have a different power in each eye or cylinder power for astigmatism. So wear only your own glasses, don't let children borrow an elder's pair, and if your own glasses feel blurry, get your power rechecked. The eye test in our store is free.
